question_en:
The Transport Museum is preparing to rearrange the Family Day display for the motorcycles in the photo: vehicles with an engine displacement not exceeding 250 cc will be placed on low platforms for easy viewing by children, while the remaining vehicles will be placed on high platforms. Count only physical motorcycles whose display signs can be matched to the vehicle, or whose foreground registration numbers are complete, legible, and uniquely identify the vehicle; do not count wall pictures, glass reflections, or partial vehicles that cannot be uniquely identified. Please answer the following questions:

1. Which motorcycles appear one by one in the photo? What are their respective engine displacements? Please list them in a table. Which motorcycles should be placed on the low platform? Which should be placed on the high platform?

The answer must include a 'Motorcycle–Engine Displacement–Platform' table, followed by separate lists of motorcycles to be placed on the low platform and the high platform.
answer:

| F004 | McKenzie (1924) | 170 | Low Platform |
| F005 | Wee McGregor / Wee MacGregor (1923) | 170 | Low Platform |
| F006 | BSA A10 Golden Flash (1955) | 646 | High Platform |
| F007 | BSA C15 (1962) | 249 (nominally 250) | Low Platform |

Low Platform: F001, F002, F003, F004, F005, F007.

High Platform: F006, F008, F009, F010, F011.
